newsitem.title: POLAND: POLE ARRESTED OVER HEROIN SMUGGLING TO BRITAIN.
newsitem.headline: POLE ARRESTED OVER HEROIN SMUGGLING TO BRITAIN.

text.p: Polish prosecutors have arrested a man suspected of belonging to a gang which tried to smuggle 92 kg of heroin into Britain last month in a coach carrying Polish soccer fans, they said on Thursday.

"The suspect says he is not guilty but we have enough evidence to say that he is and that he belonged to an organised group," Malgorzata Wilkosz-Sliwa, a prosecutor in the southern city of Krakow, told Reuters.
The suspect, identified only as "a young Polish citizen," was arrested on Wednesday by officers of the State Security Bureau (UOP) in Krakow.
Wilkosz-Sliwa said the arrested man had organised a trip and rented a coach for Polish soccer fans who came to Britain for the October 9 World Cup match between England and Poland.
The heroin was found, as the group was coming back from the game, in two cylinders running the length of the coach chassis during a routine search at Dover docks in southeast England.
Wilkosz-Sliwa said the drug came from an Asian country and that its planned destination had been England.
"Poland has become a transit country for drug smuggling ...while destination countries include Italy, Benelux states and recently Great Britain," she said.
The suspected man, if convicted, faces between three and 15 years in prison. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
